subject: computer-science
promptStrong: Give me a challenging GCSE exam-style question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the AQA spec.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for GCSE AQA Computer Science simply, with an example and the most common mistake.

questions.q: Which data type is most appropriate to store the value True or False?
questions.explain: A Boolean can only hold one of two values, True or False. AQA lists the core data types as integer, real, Boolean, character and string.

questions.q: A program stores a person's height in metres, e.g. 1.73. Which data type is most suitable?
questions.explain: A height like 1.73 has a fractional part, so a real (sometimes called float) is needed. An integer could only store whole numbers.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a variable and a constant?
options: There is no difference; the words mean the same thing
A constant's value can change while the program runs; a variable's cannot
A variable is always an integer; a constant is always a string
A variable's value can change while the program runs; a constant's value cannot
questions.explain: A constant is assigned a value once and cannot be changed during execution, whereas a variable can be reassigned. Named constants make code clearer and easier to maintain.

questions.q: What is the result of 17 MOD 5?
questions.explain: MOD gives the remainder of integer division. 17 divided by 5 is 3 remainder 2, so 17 MOD 5 = 2 (and 17 DIV 5 = 3).

questions.q: What is the result of 23 DIV 4?
questions.explain: DIV gives the whole-number (integer) part of the division. 23 / 4 = 5.75, so the integer quotient 23 DIV 4 = 5 (the remainder, 23 MOD 4, would be 3).

questions.q: Which programming construct repeats a block of code a fixed, known number of times?
questions.explain: A count-controlled (definite) loop such as FOR i to 5 repeats a set number of times. A WHILE loop is condition-controlled (indefinite) and runs until a condition changes.

questions.q: A REPEAT ... UNTIL loop tests its condition at the END of the loop. What does this guarantee?
options: The loop body always executes at least once
The loop always runs exactly twice
questions.explain: Because the condition is checked after the body runs, a REPEAT...UNTIL (post-condition) loop always executes its body at least once, unlike a WHILE loop which may run zero times.

questions.q: For x = 7, which condition evaluates to True?
questions.explain: x >= 7 is True and x <= 10 is True, and AND requires both to be True, so the whole condition is True. The others are all False for x = 7.

questions.q: Which operator would you use to test that two values are NOT equal?
questions.explain: The not-equal-to relational operator (written != or the not-equals sign depending on language) is True when the two values differ. = tests equality.

questions.q: An array names holds Ali, Bea, Cai, Dev using zero-based indexing. What does names[2] contain?
questions.explain: With zero-based indexing the first element is index 0, so index 2 is the third element, Cai. A common mistake is to read index 2 as the second element.

questions.q: How does a record differ from a one-dimensional array?
options: A record groups related fields that may be of different data types
A record must always be exactly 8 items long
A record cannot be given a name
A record can only store numbers
questions.explain: A record groups related fields (e.g. make: String, price: Real, noOfDoors: Integer) that can have different data types. A basic array normally holds items of the same type.

questions.q: What is the main difference between a function and a procedure?
options: A procedure always returns a value; a function never does
There is no difference in AQA pseudo-code
A function returns a value to the calling code; a procedure need not
questions.explain: A function returns a value to the routine that called it, whereas a procedure carries out a task without necessarily returning a value. Both are types of subroutine.

questions.q: What is a parameter?
options: The name of the whole program
A permanent value that can never change
An error produced at compile time
A value passed into a subroutine when it is called
questions.explain: A parameter is data passed into a subroutine so it can work on different values each time it is called. AQA uses the term parameter to cover both parameters and arguments.

questions.q: Which statement about a local variable is correct?
options: It is another name for a constant
It is stored permanently on the hard disk
It usually only exists while its subroutine is executing and is only accessible inside it
It can be accessed from anywhere in the whole program
questions.explain: Local variables normally exist only while the subroutine runs and can only be used inside that subroutine. This avoids clashes and is good practice in structured programming.

questions.q: Which is an advantage of the structured (modular) approach to programming?
options: It makes programs harder to read on purpose
It removes the need for any testing
It forces every variable to be global
Breaking a problem into subroutines makes code easier to write, test, reuse and maintain
questions.explain: Splitting a problem into well-documented modules with clear interfaces (parameters, return values, local variables) makes code easier to develop, test, reuse and maintain.

questions.q: If word = COMPUTER, what is the LENGTH of the string?
questions.explain: LENGTH returns the number of characters. COMPUTER has 8 letters, so LENGTH is 8.

questions.q: Concatenation of the strings CS and 50 produces which result?
options: An error, because you cannot join text and digits
questions.explain: Concatenation joins strings end to end, giving CS50. It is not addition: 50 here is a string of characters, not the number 50.

questions.q: A field must accept only values from 1 to 10. Which validation check is most appropriate?
options: A type check that only allows text
questions.explain: A range check confirms the value lies within given limits (here 1 to 10). Boundary test data such as 0, 1, 10 and 11 would be used to test it.

questions.q: A program runs but produces the wrong output; the code follows all language rules. What type of error is this?
questions.explain: A logic error means the code is valid and runs but does not do what was intended, giving incorrect results. A syntax error breaks the rules of the language and stops it running.

questions.q: Which SQL statement retrieves the Name column for every pupil in Year 11 from a table called Pupils?
options: FROM Pupils SELECT WHERE Year = 11 Name
GET Name IN Pupils IF Year = 11
SELECT Name FROM Pupils WHERE Year = 11
questions.explain: SQL SELECT queries follow SELECT fields FROM table WHERE condition. So SELECT Name FROM Pupils WHERE Year = 11 returns the required names.
